newsitem.title: USA: U.S. dealers take 5-10 cts protection new-crop soy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. dealers take 5-10 cts protection new-crop soy.

text.p: In anticipation of a lower opening in new-crop CBOT soybean and corn futures, U.S.grain dealers were taking five to 10 cents per bushel protection on new crop soybeans and three to five cents on corn.
"We're taking a dime on the beans and three cents on old and new corn," said one Ohio dealer.
CBOT new crop soybeans were expected to open lower in response to a higher-than-expected acreage forecast from the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
USDA put 1997/98 (Aug/Sep) soybean acreage at 70.9 million acres, which compared with the average trade estimate of 68.4 million.
July corn futures were expected to open one to two cents per bushel lower on a higher-than-expected quarterly stocks figure of 2.490 billion bushels, traders said.
